finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: attacker-supplied $_POST['feed'] is passed unvalidated to file_get_contents(), which fetches arbitrary URLs (http, https, ftp, file, php wrappers). Response size is echoed back, making it a blind/partially blind SSRF with a size oracle.
finding.source: $_POST['feed'] (import.php:11-12), supplied by any remote HTTP client with no authentication

trace.note: Branch entered on POST with isset($_POST['feed']); no session or admin check precedes it
strlen($xml) echoed to the caller; response size is the only data returned

finding.guards_checked: None. No require_admin() call, no scheme allowlist, no host/IP denylist, no redirect control, no timeout. allow_url_fopen is PHP default-on; php.ini not present in repo so could not confirm. Contrast: set_webhook branch calls require_admin() at line 18, so this branch departs from the file's pattern.

verdict.guard_found: none. The POST feed branch (import.php:11-12) has no require_admin() call, scheme allowlist, or host check before file_get_contents(). The only require_admin() call is at import.php:18, inside the set_webhook branch, which the candidate correctly identified.
verdict.reason: $_POST['feed'] at import.php:11-12 reaches file_get_contents() with no authentication or validation, and import.php:13 echoes strlen($xml) back to the caller, so any remote client can drive the fetch and read the response size. Every trace line matches the file, and the grep confirms require_admin() is only called at import.php:18.

finding.claim: Admin-gated blind SSRF: $_POST['set_webhook'] is passed to curl_init()/curl_exec() with no scheme or host validation. Response body is discarded; the caller only receives 'ok'.
finding.source: $_POST['set_webhook'] (import.php:17-19), intended to be supplied only by an admin; gated by require_admin()

trace.note: require_admin() returns 403 unless $_SESSION['is_admin'] is non-empty (defined lines 4-9)
curl_init($hook) creates handle with attacker-controlled URL
CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER set but response is not used

finding.guards_checked: Admin session check only (require_admin, lines 4-9). No CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS restriction, no host/IP validation, no CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION control. How is_admin is set is not in this repository, so session hardening could not be verified. Severity lower because exploitation requires an admin session.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() at import.php:4-9 gates the branch (returns 403 unless $_SESSION['is_admin'] is non-empty). No host, scheme, or CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS validation exists before curl_init at import.php:20. The admin gate is not one of the closing guards, but it limits the source to admin sessions.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code (import.php:17-23), but the only path to $_POST['set_webhook'] requires an admin session (import.php:18, require_admin at lines 4-9), so the source is not controllable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege remote attacker, and the finding as framed does not meet the bar for CONFIRMED. Separately, import.php:11-13 is an ungated `file_get_contents($_POST['feed'])` reachable without any session, which is a stronger and unauthenticated SSRF-style issue that the candidate did not report and should be triaged on its own.
